For Harmony, our image analysis pipeline delivers 894 preselected features, whereas the analogous CellProfiler pipeline provides 3,648 features (von Coburg et al., 2025a). We showed that both pipelines are generally applicable to CPP data (von Coburg et al., 2025a). However, using CellProfiler typically requires an additional time‐consuming step for image export from proprietary microscope software data formats. Furthermore, the numerous CellProfiler features also contain higher numbers of missing or constant values, thus needing more extensive filtering of features during the data cleaning procedure, which makes using CellProfiler somewhat less practical overall. In this protocol, we therefore describe the image analysis pipeline using Harmony. For more details on CPP image analysis using CellProfiler, we refer readers to von Coburg et al. (2025a) and Wedler, Körber, & Liu (2026).

Thaw LysoBrite Component B stock solution (containing the Live Cell Staining Buffer, not including dyes; part of the Cell Navigator Lysosome Staining Kit NIR Fluorescence, AAT Bioquest, cat. no. 22652) protected from light. Mix 50 ml LysoBrite Component B with 0.5 g bovine serum albumin (BSA), low endotoxin, lyophilized powder (PAN Biotech, cat. no. P06‐139350), to generate a 1% (w/v) BSA solution. Sterile filter using a 0.22‐µm‐pore‐size filter to avoid crystals, e.g., using a bottle‐top vacuum filter system with a 0.22‐µm filter (Sigma‐Aldrich, cat. no. 430769). Aliquot the solution as needed and store at −20°C.

To prepare 50 ml of 2× cycle 1 staining and permeabilization solution, add 50 µl of 66 µM phalloidin and 6.25 µl of 5 mM SYTO14 to 50 ml of 2× basal fixed‐cell staining buffer (see recipe). Add 0.1 ml of 100% (v/v) Triton X‐100 (Sigma, cat. no. T8787) to 49.9 ml of the staining solution to obtain a 0.2% (v/v) Triton‐X concentration. Mix well and keep solution protected from light.

steps.title: Prepare assay‑ready compound plates
steps.instruction: Spot 100 nl of 1 000× compound stock (100 % DMSO) onto each well of a 384‑well plate using an acoustic liquid handler; store plates at –20 °C. On the day of the experiment add 20 µl medium to each well to generate a 5× compound solution (0.5 % [v/v] DMSO). Transfer 10 µl of this 5× solution to cells that contain 40 µl growth medium (final 1× solution, 0.1 % [v/v] DMSO). Prepare at least one plate copy per biological replicate.

steps.title: Prepare 2× basal live‑cell buffer
steps.instruction: Thaw LysoBrite Component B (Cell Navigator Lysosome Staining Kit NIR Fluorescence, AAT Bioquest, cat. no. 22652) protected from light. Mix 50 ml Component B with 0.5 g low‑endotoxin BSA (PAN Biotech, cat. no. P06‑139350) to obtain 1 % (w/v) BSA. Sterile‑filter through a 0.22 µm bottle‑top vacuum filter (Sigma‑Aldrich, cat. no. 430769). Aliquot as needed and store at –20 °C (stable 4 weeks–6 months).

steps.title: Prepare 2× basal fixed‑cell buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 100 ml Dulbecco’s Balanced Salt Solution (DPBS, PAN Biotech, cat. no. P04‑36500) with 1 g low‑endotoxin BSA (PAN Biotech, cat. no. P06‑139350) to obtain 1 % (w/v) BSA. Sterile‑filter through a 0.22 µm bottle‑top vacuum filter (Sigma‑Aldrich, cat. no. 430769). Store aliquots at 4 °C (stable up to 6 months).

steps.title: Prepare 2× live‑cell staining solution
steps.instruction: Thaw LysoBrite Component A (contains LysoBrite NIR dye) and the MitoTracker stock solution (see dye stock) protected from light; vortex briefly and spin 10 s at max speed in a tabletop centrifuge. To 49.75 ml of the 2× basal live‑cell buffer add 200 µl of 500× LysoBrite Component A and 50 µl of 1 mM MitoTracker stock. Mix well, keep protected from light, and use the solution fresh on the day of the experiment.

substeps.instruction: Calculate staining volume: 15 µl per well (≈5.76 ml per 384‑well plate) plus 7–10 ml void volume for the pipetting robot.

steps.title: Prepare 2× cycle‑1 staining & permeabilization solution
steps.instruction: Thaw phalloidin (66 µM) and SYTO14 (5 mM) stock solutions protected from light; vortex and spin 10 s at max speed. To 50 ml of the 2× basal fixed‑cell buffer add 50 µl phalloidin and 6.25 µl SYTO14. Then add 0.1 ml (100 µl) of 100 % Triton X‑100 (Sigma, cat. no. T8787) to 49.9 ml of the mixture to obtain a final 0.2 % (v/v) Triton X‑100 concentration. Mix well, protect from light, and prepare fresh on the day of use.

steps.title: Prepare 2× cycle‑2 staining solution
steps.instruction: Thaw wheat germ agglutinin (WGA) and concanavalin A (ConA) stock solutions protected from light; vortex and spin 10 s at max speed. To 50 ml of the 2× basal fixed‑cell buffer add 125 µl of 1 mg ml⁻¹ WGA, 200 µl of 5 mg ml⁻¹ ConA, and 25 µl of 10 mg ml⁻¹ Hoechst. Mix well, keep protected from light, and prepare fresh on the day of use.

steps.title: Cultivate and seed RPTEC‑TERT1 cells
steps.instruction: Maintain RPTEC‑TERT1 cells in collagen‑coated flasks with growth medium (see recipe) and passage every 2–3 days at ~80 % confluency; use cells ≤ passage 5 and keep a cryopreserved cell bank. Seed cells into collagen‑coated 384‑well plates (Greiner Bio‑One, cat. no. 781866) at a density that yields ~80 % confluency at stimulation and 2 000–2 500 cells per well. Keep the cell suspension homogeneous by mixing before and during dispensing. After seeding, let plates sit in the biosafety cabinet for 1 h before transferring to the incubator.

steps.title: Apply live‑cell staining (cycle 1) and image
steps.instruction: Add the 2× live‑cell staining solution to each well (final concentration achieved by 1:1 mixing with the existing medium). Incubate for the recommended time (as in Basic Protocol 2). Use a microplate washer for any aspiration/wash steps, setting the washer to avoid disturbing the cell layer. After staining, image the plates on an automated fluorescence microscope.

substeps.instruction: Ensure consistent pipetting across all wells; if using an automated system, test the program beforehand and verify no air is aspirated.
If processing multiple plates, complete all live‑cell staining steps on all plates before switching tips to fixation solutions.

steps.title: Elute dyes and fix/permeabilize (cycle 1)
steps.instruction: Apply the elution buffer (as described in Basic Protocol 2) to remove the first‑cycle dyes. Then add the 2× cycle‑1 staining and permeabilization solution prepared earlier, incubate as specified, and wash with the microplate washer.

steps.title: Apply cycle‑2 staining and image
steps.instruction: Add the 2× cycle‑2 staining solution to each well, incubate according to the protocol, wash with the microplate washer, and acquire images on the same automated microscope.

steps.title: Perform image analysis with Harmony
steps.instruction: In Harmony, load the acquired image sets and run the CPP analysis pipeline: execute the building blocks for Find Nuclei, Find Cytoplasm, Find Spots (Nucleoli), and any additional BBs listed in Table 3. Verify segmentation visually for each BB. Export the per‑cell feature table as a .txt file.

steps.title: Export features and run CPPAnalyzer notebook
steps.instruction: Place the exported Harmony .txt files together with Table_to_exclude_wells.xlsx, Compound_layout.xlsx, and Table_planes.xlsx in the input folder structure shown in Fig. 1C. Launch the CPPAnalyzer Jupyter notebook, set Nucleoli = TRUE and Featag = "Cells", and run the notebook. Use propNAfea = 0.15 to exclude features with ≥15 % missing values and propNAcell = 0 to discard any cell containing a missing value.

steps.title: Conduct BMC modeling in KNIME workflow
steps.instruction: Open the automated CPPManager KNIME workflow (Basic Protocol 5). The workflow will import the cleaned data, fit dose‑response curves for each feature using the R package tpclfit 2 with the five models cnst, hill, poly1, poly2, and pow, and select the best fit to calculate the benchmark concentration (BMC). Features with BMC > BMChigh are marked inactive; if BMC < BMClow, adjust BMC to the modified lowest concentration using log10BMCLOW = log10(lowesttestedconc.) − 0.5.

steps.title: Filter and categorize BMC results
steps.instruction: Enable BMC filtering to remove entries with hit‑call ≤0.9, missing BMDU/BMDL, or BMC > BMChigh. Group the remaining features into predefined categories (Supporting Table 3). Declare a feature category active when ≥30 % of its features have a valid BMC, then generate accumulation and magnitude plots as described.
